item.title: Methodological Heterogeneity and Predictor Omission in the BLISS Prognostic Score for COPD Respiratory Admissions
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, We read with great interest the study by Jordan et al. [1] describing the development and validation of the BLISS prognostic score for predicting two-year respiratory admissions among patients with chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD) in primary care. item.title: Tetris and PTSD symptoms: a medical perspective on benefits, limits, and escalation
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Adam Grant’s Hidden Potential book (1) captures how many clinicians first hear about “Tetris for trauma”: a vivid anecdote that a simple visuospatial game, played soon after distressing material, can reduce later flashbacks, paired with a sensible warning that a game is not a cure for PTSD. item.title: Regulating dermatology advice from social media influencers
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The recent BMJ article on digital misinformation from social media as a recent public health challenge highlights the role of influencers and celebrities as a growing source of patient information. Social media creators now form the basis of many patient decisions before they ever seek medical advice from licensed practitioners. item.title: Re: Matt Morgan: Why is stopping a pointless intervention so difficult?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor I share many of the same frustrations as the author with persistence of pointless interventions just because "that's what we do and we always have". I would temper his frustration with a recognition of the limitations of a randomised controlled trial. Once cited as the absolute pinnacle of evidence based medicine we are now learning that, as always, real life is usually more complicated. item.title: Re: Partha Kar: Expanding roles of healthcare staff—where are the safety checks?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Author raises legitimate concerns about supervision, regulation, and patient transparency in the expansion of non-physician roles within healthcare systems. Patient safety should remain the central organising principle of any workforce redesign. However, framing role expansion primarily as a dilution of medical expertise risks misunderstanding the structural realities of modern healthcare. item.title: Re: Doctors’ pay fell more than public sector average over 14 years, analysis shows
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, It is important to note as the article that the Doctors’ pay has declined in real terms over the past 15 years, with resident doctors down 8.6% and consultants down 10% from 2011 earnings.
